senses.definition: Any substance, especially food, used in catching fish, or other animals, by alluring them to a hook, snare, trap, or net.
Food containing poison or a harmful additive to kill animals that are pests.
Anything which allures; something or someone used to lure or entice someone or something into doing something.

quotes.text: One of the “girls” used in this way, Pamella Bordes, later spoke of being “part of an enormous group … used as sexual bait.”
quotes.reference: 2017 June 7, Adam Lusher, “Adnan Khashoggi: the 'whoremonger' whose arms deals funded a playboy life of decadence and 'pleasure wives'”, in The Independent, London:

subsenses.definition: (as the head of a compound) Something that lures or entices a specified group.
(vulgar, sexuality) Someone that attracts or entices a specified sex act being done to them.

senses.definition: A portion of food or drink, as a refreshment taken on a journey; also, a stop for rest and refreshment.

quotes.text: A short stop, but no refreshment. Such baits are frequently given by the natives of the principality to their keffels, or horses, particularly after climbing a hill.

subsenses.definition: (Geordie, Durham) A packed lunch - the bite to eat a worker took with them to eat.
(East Anglia) A small meal taken mid-morning while farming.

senses.definition: (Internet slang) A post intended to elicit a, usually strong or negative, reaction from others.
examples: Please stop posting bait, or I will have to mute you.

senses.definition: (transitive) To attract with bait; to entice.
(transitive) To affix bait to a trap or a fishing hook or fishing line.

senses.definition: (transitive) To lay baits in an environment to control pest species.
(transitive) To target a pest species by laying baits.
(transitive) To set dogs on (an animal etc.) to bite or worry; to attack with dogs, especially for sport.
examples: to bait a bear with dogs

senses.definition: (transitive) To intentionally annoy, torment, or threaten by constant rebukes or threats; to harass.
